changes.historical_text: FLIP: You can return up to 2 Monster Cards from the field to the owner's hand.
changes.summary: Period trigger semantics with no text correlate: the GOAT variant registers the FLIP effect as a forced trigger (EFFECT_TYPE_TRIGGER_F, and without EFFECT_FLAG_DELAY) whose target selection accepts 0 to 2 monsters, so flipping Penguin Soldier compels the effect to activate while the controller may return nothing (upstream annotation: 'Forced trigger, but can select 0 targets'). The modern script is an optional trigger (EFFECT_TYPE_TRIGGER_O + EFFECT_FLAG_DELAY) that needs at least 1 target to activate. Both keep EFFECT_FLAG_CARD_TARGET, so targeting itself is unchanged. Chronology is unresolved: nothing in the packet dates when the trigger stopped being mandatory or when the 0-target selection was withdrawn.

review.notes: Baseline implements lineage v0 (SDJ-022, Starter Deck: Joey, earliest TCG 2003-03-01) exactly. The whole English lineage v0 -> v4 (YS12-EN015, 2012-04-13) is wording only: v1/v2/v3 alternate between 'the owner's hand' and 'their owners' hands', and v4 is the PSCT rewrite 'target up to 2 monsters on the field; return those targets to the hand'. The modern script's minimum of 1 target correlates with that v4 PSCT rewrite, but nothing in the packet ties the change to that printing, and the forced-vs-optional difference has no text correlate at all ('You can' appears in both v0 and v4) - so the whole script-level package is recorded as one ruling change with unresolved chronology rather than dated to YS12. Not listed on EdisonFormat.com's Functional Errata page.
